consequence.explanation: You matched the account route to the young account holder and checked an identity document option. Real banks set the exact requirements; never enter real personal or financial details in this game.

claim.documents: RBI's KYC Direction lists multiple officially valid document (OVD) options for identity and address checks, including passport, driving licence, voter ID, an MGNREGA job card, an NPR letter, and Aadhaar-related proof, subject to the applicable rules.
claim.aadhaar: Aadhaar is not the only OVD listed in RBI's KYC Direction. Whether a document is accepted depends on the financial service and applicable requirements; Aadhaar is not universally compulsory for every financial task.
claim.minors: RBI's KYC Direction has a separate requirement for a customer whose account was opened while they were a minor and who has now become an adult: the bank must obtain a fresh photograph and confirm current KYC documents, and may redo KYC where required.

wrong_document.review: Your choice: you selected an account route that does not match the person's age. Safer choice: choose the minor route for a minor and the adult route for an adult; check the bank's minor-account and guardian process. Concept: minors' accounts have distinct operating conditions. Why it matters: age and safeguards affect who can operate the account.

Your choice: you selected an unsupported identity-document route. Safer choice: check the accepted OVDs for the task; a passport or voter ID can be an option, while a school library card is not an OVD. Do not assume Aadhaar is the only option. Concept: KYC has more than one document route. Why it matters: the wrong document can delay access, and assuming Aadhaar is always required can wrongly block it.
